## Summary — 2026-09-02 run

**Starting state check:** Account equity $97,383.92. `get_all_positions` showed four existing option holdings: AVGO, DELL, HPE, PANW — all long back-month calls with **no offsetting short front leg**. `get_orders(closed)` explained why: minutes before this session, buy-to-close orders had already filled on the front legs of all four (AVGO260904C00370000, HPE260904C00052000, DELL260904C00470000, PANW260904C00360000) — the front-leg-within-2-days-of-expiry roll trigger had fired and the "close" half of the roll was done, leaving each position as a naked long call.

**Roll completions (AVGO, HPE):** Both tickers are still flagged Tier A / candidate=true today with a live front/back date pair, so I completed the roll by selling a new front-month ATM call against the already-held back leg:
- Checked live chain + open interest on the target front contracts: AVGO260904C00347500 (OI 20, bid/ask 25.62/28.13, mid 26.875 — matches scan) and HPE260904C00047500 (OI 118, bid/ask 5.44/5.70, mid 5.57 — matches scan). Both cleared the >10 OI and reasonable-spread bars.
- Sold to open: 4x AVGO260904C00347500 @ 26.50 limit, and 18x HPE260904C00047500 @ 5.50 limit (both priced just inside mid, aggressive side, per the fill-discipline rule). Orders were accepted but landed right at/after the close, so they're queued as day orders for the next session rather than filled immediately — will need to check tomorrow whether they filled or need repricing against the fresh open.
- Note for the record: rolling the front strike down to today's ATM (347.5 / 47.5) while the back leg sits at its original, now-stale strike (370 / 52) turns these into diagonals rather than pure same-strike calendars for the remainder of this cycle. That's an accepted byproduct of weekly-rolling the short leg while holding the long leg through to its own expiry/event — flagging it explicitly since it changes the risk shape from "capped at debit paid" to a diagonal with modest short-term delta mismatch. Worth a second look once we know if these fill.

**DELL, PANW:** Also left as naked long back-month calls after today's front close, but neither appears in today's scan output, so there's no earnings-aware date/strike to roll into. Per the rule against re-deriving scan logic myself, I left these untouched — they're currently just directional long calls, not actioned.

**New candidates evaluated (NTAP, LULU, ZS) — all skipped, no new positions opened:**
- **LULU**: front leg (121C, Sep4) fine — OI 234, tight spread. But back leg (121C, Oct2) had **OI = 8**, under the 10 threshold, plus a stale last trade and a ~15% wide spread. Skipped — back leg wouldn't reliably fill as part of a two-leg combo.
- **ZS**: front leg (172.5C, Sep4) fine — OI 53. Back leg (172.5C, Oct2) had **OI = 1** — essentially no market. Clear skip.
- **NTAP**: front (165C, Sep18) OI 820 fine, but back leg (165C, Oct16) had OI 17 with only 1 trade printed that day and a ~15% wide spread, stale close price. Technically above the raw "10" cutoff but thin enough in practice (both by OI and spread) that I treated it as a skip rather than force a two-leg fill.

**Position count:** Still 4 tickers held (AVGO, DELL, HPE, PANW) — well within the 6-8 cap — since no new names were added today.

**Bottom line:** Completed the two overdue front-leg rolls that the risk rules require (AVGO, HPE), left DELL/PANW alone pending fresh scan data, and passed on all three fresh Tier-A candidates today because every one of them had an illiquid back leg (OI at or near single digits) even though the net mid pricing looked clean — exactly the "clean price, unfillable spread" trap the rules warn about.
